english_lines: A tough one for guarding — this khaki-shirt man,
He is a fellow from Thanjavur district,
A warrior made with a fearless heart,
He will say, 'We will do what we said,'
He will say only what he actually did,
He will conduct himself so as to be trusted,
He will work for our country,
He will not take mamool,
He will not hate good people,
He will say conscience is God,
He will serve our people,
(A tough one for guarding).
notes: The police-song register remains colloquial: `காக்கிச்சட்டைக்காரன்` is kept as `khaki-shirt man` rather than formalized as police officer.
`மாமூலு` remains `mamool`, preserving the source's culturally specific bribe/regular-payment term.
The paired `சொன்னதை செய்வோம் / செய்ததையே சொல்வோம்` formulation remains explicit instead of being summarized as honesty.

english_lines: When the fence itself grazes the crop — that,
He will not bear that pain,
He will not be a vengai,
Pouncing upon a white goat,
If the gang that brews illicit liquor,
Comes asking him for support,
By truth, he will flare up,
He will strike with the whip,
Hoarding and smuggling,
He will tear them into cotton-fluff, cotton-fluff,
(A tough one for guarding).
notes: The proverb-image `வேலியே பயிரை மேயும்` remains literally the fence grazing the crop.
`வேங்கை` remains `vengai`, keeping the tiger/tree-associated heroic image rather than forcing a single English equivalent.
The illicit-liquor `support` code-mixing and the violent colloquial `பஞ்சு பஞ்சா பிச்சிடுவான்` are retained as source-shaped speech, not softened into bureaucratic anti-smuggling language.

translator_notes: The lyric idealizes a police figure through colloquial speech, anti-bribery language and proverb-like violence against corruption. The English retains that register rather than converting it into formal civic prose.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
